tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative phrasing ('Use this skill when the user wants...'), focuses on user intent and symptoms (high bill, drift, throttling, quota headroom) rather than internal implementation, explicitly lists many trigger contexts including cases where the user doesn't name the domain directly (e.g. 'why the bill is high', 'tokens billed at $0'), and ends with a clear exclusion. While long, it is a single dense paragraph appropriate for the breadth of triggers it needs to cover, and remains within the bounds of a concise description for a complex domain skill.
tests.evidence: Use this skill when the user wants to understand or cut Amazon Bedrock spend, or check Bedrock capacity, even if they don't call it a cost review, for example why the bill is high or suspiciously low...

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body is dense with domain-specific rules (billed vs estimated labeling, exact APIs, quota naming conventions) and avoids explaining general concepts the agent already knows. It stays focused on non-obvious Bedrock cost/capacity specifics.
tests.evidence: 'Usage types vary (-mantle-, -standard, -flex, -priority, -cross-region-global): match a model's lines loosely.' — this is project-specific, not general knowledge.

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: Detailed reference data (quota codes, API quirks, metric details, check catalog) are largely in references/ files and linked conditionally; the body table in the Check Families section is a concise summary (check-id, detects, severity) rather than full remediation text, which is acceptable as a lookup index.
tests.evidence: 'Detection rules, remediations, citations: [cost-analysis.md](references/cost-analysis.md) ... Check Families of other skills ... are never raised here.'

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: All 8 files in references/ are linked via markdown links in the body (cost-analysis.md, checks-model-invocation.md, cloudwatch-alarm-reference.md, collection-reference.md, metrics-and-logs.md, api-quirks.md, quota-codes.md, related-skills.md).

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Reference links consistently specify when to load them, tied to specific steps or conditions.
tests.evidence: 'Load when the step says so: [cost-analysis.md](references/cost-analysis.md) (Steps 3–5, before any LLM-COST or LLM-PT finding)'

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference links use relative paths rooted at references/ with no absolute paths or traversal.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile/consistency-critical operations (cost labeling, quota lookup, read-only rules) are given exact, prescriptive steps, while flexible judgment calls (deciding COST-003/004 applicability) are described with reasoning rather than rigid scripts.
tests.evidence: 'Read-only. Never create, resize or delete Provisioned Throughput...' is prescriptive for a fragile rule, while 'decide 003/004 from the invocation pattern and the stated workload' allows judgment.

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: Where multiple data sources exist (rates), a clear priority order is given rather than a flat menu.
tests.evidence: 'Rates, in order: the user (say so); pricing:GetProducts ... or the pricing page read with verify_aws_claim.'

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The skill teaches a generalizable procedure (scope, tokens, cost model, coverage check, checks, PT, headroom, alarms) applicable to any Bedrock cost/capacity review, not a one-off instance.
tests.evidence: 'Run the steps in order. Each step is bounded: a denied API, no datapoints or an unsupported region is recorded as unavailable ...'

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The skill has an extensive 'Common wrong answers' section and 'Error Handling' section documenting concrete, non-obvious pitfalls specific to this domain.
tests.evidence: '"A us. profile bills as us-east-1." It is a geographic routing scope; billing follows the source region (api-quirks §14, LLM-COST-005).'

tests.name: Validation loops
tests.reasoning: The skill includes an explicit self-validation section instructing the agent to check its own output against rules before presenting.
tests.evidence: '## Before You Present — Validate Your Own Output\n\nA confidently wrong cost number is worse than a slow one. If an item can't be met, say so.'
